partners.mechanism_chain: SEC23A (HGNC:10394) —DISRUPTS→ COPII vesicle trafficking; COPII vesicle trafficking —DECREASES→ Lysosomal enzyme delivery to lysosome; Lysosomal enzyme delivery to lysosome —DECREASES→ Glycoprotein catabolism; Glycoprotein catabolism —LEADS_TO→ Craniolenticulosutural dysplasia phenotype (MONDO:0011911); CTSA (HGNC:2406) —DISRUPTS→ Beta-galactosidase activity and stability; Beta-galactosidase activity and stability —DECREASES→ Glycoprotein catabolism; Glycoprotein catabolism —LEADS_TO→ GM1 and GM2 ganglioside accumulation (HP:0002172); GM1 and GM2 ganglioside accumulation (HP:0002172) —LEADS_TO→ Galactosialidosis phenotype (MONDO:0009737). #### 1. galactosialidosis  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.449)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2132295)

**Proposed mechanism:** SEC23A (HGNC:10394) —DISRUPTS→ COPII vesicle trafficking; COPII vesicle trafficking —DECREASES→ Lysosomal enzyme delivery to lysosome; Lysosomal enzyme delivery to lysosome —DECREASES→ Glycoprotein catabolism; Glycoprotein catabolism —LEADS_TO→ Craniolenticulosutural dysplasia phenotype (MONDO:0011911); CTSA (HGNC:2406) —DISRUPTS→ Beta-galactosidase activity and stability; Beta-galactosidase activity and stability —DECREASES→ Glycoprotein catabolism; Glycoprotein catabolism —LEADS_TO→ GM1 and GM2 ganglioside accumulation (HP:0002172); GM1 and GM2 ganglioside accumulation (HP:0002172) —LEADS_TO→ Galactosialidosis phenotype (MONDO:0009737). Similarly, defects in CTSA lead to reduced beta-galactosidase activity, also impairing glycoprotein catabolism and causing galactosialidosis. The convergence is on the shared pathway of glycoprotein catabolism, which is affected by deficiencies in the delivery of multiple lysosomal hydrolases due to SEC23A dysfunction, and by the specific loss of beta-galactosidase activity due to CTSA deficiency.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic studies demonstrate that SEC23A mutations in craniolenticulosutural dysplasia do not impair the delivery or function of any lysosomal hydrolases involved in glycoprotein catabolism, or if CTSA mutations in galactosialidosis do not lead to accumulation of substrates processed by lysosomal hydrolases, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: Absence of pathogenic variants in SEC23A and CTSA in relevant populations within gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding this overlap could suggest that therapeutic strategies aimed at improving lysosomal enzyme delivery or function might be beneficial for both craniolenticulosutural dysplasia and galactosialidosis, potentially through gene therapy or small molecule approaches that stabilize lysosomal enzymes or enhance their transport.
